question.text: What happens to a trader's open position if they don't close it before the expiry of the contract?

answer.text: The position is settled at the final settlement price (FBIL reference rate) through cash settlement
The position is automatically rolled over to the next month's contract
The trader must take physical delivery of the currency
The position is cancelled with no profit or loss

explanation.text: The Logic: Open futures positions on the last trading day are marked to the Final Settlement Price and settled in cash; current exchange-traded currency derivatives are cash settled in INR (p. 166). The Trap: Exchange-traded currency futures do NOT auto-rollover and do not require physical delivery. Open positions cease after expiration (p. 168). Note: To maintain exposure beyond expiry, the trader must manually close the expiring contract and open a position in the next contract.
